title: Potential difference

draft.title: Potential difference
card: Potential difference (p.d.), also called voltage, is the energy each coulomb of charge gains or loses between two points in a circuit. It is measured in volts (V).
V = E/q, where E is energy in joules and q is charge in coulombs. So 1 volt means 1 joule of energy for each coulomb.
A battery or power supply gives energy to the charge. A component such as a lamp or resistor changes that energy into other forms, such as heat and light, so the charge loses energy there.
A bigger p.d. means more energy for every coulomb. For a given charge, E = qV.
draft.remember: Voltage is energy per coulomb: 1 V is 1 J for each 1 C.

a.q: A lamp has a potential difference of 6 V across it. What does this tell you about the charge passing through it?
opts: Each coulomb transfers 6 J of energy in the lamp
Each second, 6 C of charge passes through the lamp
The lamp transfers 6 J of energy every second
The lamp holds 6 C of charge stored inside it
a.why: 6 V means 6 joules for each coulomb, so each coulomb loses 6 J as it passes through the lamp. The option about 6 J every second mixes up energy per coulomb with energy per second, which is not what a volt measures.
a.clue: A volt is a measure of energy for each coulomb.

b.q: Mia's phone charger supplies charge at 5 V. How much energy is given to 20 C of charge by the charger?
b.why: E = qV = 20 C × 5 V = 100 J. The answer 4 J comes from dividing charge by voltage, which turns the relationship upside down.
b.clue: Multiply the charge by the energy given to each coulomb.

a.best: Each coulomb transfers 6 J of energy in the lamp
